basis: X = tan(theta/2), full circle Fourier (the target is NON-symmetric)

instrument_limit_roundtrip.what: X -> theta -> X relative defect, the bound on the domain ladder's reach
instrument_limit_roundtrip.note: this is why NB-3 stops at X_max = 3.0e+05: the map itself, not the physics, is what runs out of digits

positive_control_clm_anchor.what: Omega_0 = -sin theta = -2X/(1+X^2): exactly one basis mode, p = infinity
positive_control_clm_anchor.can_fail: a wrong half-angle convention, a sign error in theta_of_X or an off-by-one in the FFT phase all smear this across every k

negative_control_1_inverse_X.what: Omega = 1/(1+|X|): far field |X|^-1, kink at theta = pi, p = 2 exactly
negative_control_1_inverse_X.why_p2_matters: p = 2 is the divergence threshold of the class s = 1 -- the class leg 51 measured the operator to be least bad in, and the class the ban clause names
negative_control_1_inverse_X.note_even_modes_annihilated: h(theta) + h(pi - theta) = 1 kills every even mode; this control is retained BECAUSE that broke two versions of the fitter

negative_control_2_sawtooth.what: Omega = 2 arctan(X)/pi, i.e. h(theta) = theta/pi: alpha = 0, a JUMP
negative_control_2_sawtooth.why_p1_matters: p = 1 is the divergence threshold of the FLAT class s = 0
negative_control_2_sawtooth.note: this control brackets the target's alpha-cusp from the BAD side: a jump is the worst non-smoothness on the circle, so if the instrument holds here it holds for any 0 < alpha < 1

calibration_family.what: Omega_alpha = (1+X^2)^{-alpha/2}: far field exactly |X|^-alpha, h = |cos(theta/2)|^alpha, so p = 1 + alpha for every alpha
calibration_family.role: this is the instrument's systematic error bar AT THE HEADLINE'S OWN TRANSFORM SIZE, and it is what the target's exponent must be quoted against.  The bias is POSITIVE -- the fitter over-estimates p -- so a bias-corrected exponent is LOWER than the quoted one
calibration_family.why_M_matters: at M = 65536 the finest theta cell reaches |X| = 2M/pi = 4.17e+04, past the headline domain's X_max, so that grid could not have been used for the target without extrapolating.  The calibration family is analytic and has no such limit, which is exactly why calibrating it on a finer grid than the target was measured on flatters the instrument

NB2_resolution_ladder.what: n = 201/401/801 at the shipped domain rho_max = 8, X_max = 745
NB2_resolution_ladder.reading: the resolution ladder is FLAT -- p moves by less than the fitter's own systematic.  The exponent is not resolution limited at this domain size; it is DOMAIN limited, which is NB-3

NB3_domain_ladder.what: X_max = 745 -> 3.0e+05.  This is a DIAGNOSTIC on whether the measured exponent is a property of the profile or of the domain; it is NOT an attempt to close the certificate's truncation gap, which is a different quantity and is separately banned
NB3_domain_ladder.reading: p - 1 and the physical-space tail exponent RISE TOGETHER toward alpha as X_max grows.  At X_max = 745 the profile has not yet reached its asymptotic tail, and the coefficient measurement reports the effective exponent over the range it can see -- agreeing with the independent physical-space fit over the same range.  Two different measurements of the same shortfall
NB3_domain_ladder.relation_to_leg_47: leg 47 measured that extending the domain makes the certificate's TRUNCATION GAP worse (+0.47 decades per unit rho).  That is not contradicted: the exponent improves with reach while the gap worsens.  Different quantities, and nothing here repairs the gap

far_field_closure.can_change_the_answer: 'clamp' injects alpha = 0 and 'zero' injects a jump, both worth a spurious k^-1; if they moved p the measurement would be reporting the closure and not the profile

interpolation_order.why_the_second_column_is_here: p is identical to five digits across orders 2..12, and identical numbers are exactly what lesson 90 says to distrust.  So the movement of the INTERPOLANT ITSELF is reported beside it: order 2 shifts h by 8.7e-05 relative and shifts p by 3.5e-05.  The knob is wired and the profile is resolved -- that is a real null, not a tautology of the code

analytic_tail.reason: p - s <= 1: the weighted sum diverges; the tail has no value

NB5_norms.reading: the partial sums are not the norm.  What makes the norm finite is the TAIL, and the tail is a statement about p: finite iff p - s > 1.  Where it is not, the entry says so instead of quoting a large number

NB6_second_unknown.what: a certificate needs BOTH unknowns in the space.  The steady equation forces Omega ~ |X|^(c_omega/c_l) and V ~ |X|^(2 c_omega/c_l), so V should decay TWICE as fast and be the easier of the two
NB6_second_unknown.reading: V is the easier unknown by roughly a factor two in the exponent, so Omega is what sets the admissible window and the gate is decided on Omega alone
